# TeshuvaDraft — [Sacred-text scholarship / Judaism — rabbis and poskim]
**Claim:** A drafting workbench for ordained rabbis writing teshuvot (responsa) that auto-assembles a structured precedent brief — Hebrew/Aramaic source passages, prior responsa from Bar Ilan and Sefaria, machloket rishonim/acharonim — given the rabbi's question framing, so the rabbi spends time on psak (ruling) and argumentation rather than manual source-hunting across a 30-volume library.
**Why-now capability:** Sefaria's documented MCP server (2025-2026) enables live structured retrieval from its 3,000+ text corpus without a custom RAG pipeline. Multilingual Hebrew/Aramaic LLM instruction-following (GPT-4o, Claude 3.7) is now reliable enough to parse a rabbinic question in Hebrew and generate a sourced precedent structure — not psak, only source discovery — a task that failed with earlier models due to Aramaic hallucination.
**Mechanism / rationale:** The self-handicapped incumbent pattern: every verified Jewish AI product (TorahWiz, RavAI, Rebbe.io, DafBuddy, ChavrutAI, Hevruta AI, Mishneh AI) targets the learner. Sefaria's own AI policy explicitly states it will not answer halachic questions, only textual ones. Bar Ilan Responsa (the gold-standard scholarly database) is a Windows-only USB install with no AI layer and no API. The rabbi who writes actual responsa has no AI drafting tool — only a search engine. Payer: ordained rabbis (Conservative, Modern Orthodox, Orthodox) who write responsa professionally ($39-79/month); also seminaries (YU, JTS, HUC) as institutional licenses. Compounding-corpus wedge: TeshuvaDraft accumulates each rabbi's past teshuvot as private context, learning each posek's reasoning style and preferred authorities, making switching costly.
**Novelty:** All verified competitors serve lay learners seeking educational explanation. None provide a professional drafting tool for the ordained rabbi who will sign a teshuvah. A learner tool explains what Rambam said; a drafting tool assembles a structured argument scaffold the rabbi edits, challenges, and takes halakhic responsibility for. Rabbi Dr. Aaron Glatt's documented assessment names source-gathering as the legitimate AI use case — this fills exactly that gap.
**Test:** Recruit 8 rabbis (Orthodox, Conservative) currently writing responsa. 60-day beta providing source briefs for their next 3 teshuvot each. Measure: (a) reported time savings on source assembly, (b) source recall (fraction of cited sources TeshuvaDraft surfaced), (c) hallucination rate (false citations, verified against Bar Ilan). Success: >40% time savings, >60% source recall, <5% citation hallucination.
**Assumptions:** (1) Sefaria MCP coverage of responsa literature is sufficient; the Bar Ilan gap is documented and disclosed. (2) Rabbis accept the tool produces source scaffolds only — all psak is the rabbi's sole responsibility (reinforced in UI). (3) Hebrew/Aramaic retrieval accuracy requires a Hebrew-literate engineer or rabbinic consultant. Crisis-safety: not applicable. Licensing: Sefaria texts are CC-licensed; Bar Ilan integration would require partnership or alternative corpus.
